([[Cary, North Carolina]]) | college = * [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]] (2018–2020) * [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2020–2021) | highlights = }} '''Kenneth "Trey" Murphy III''' (born June 18, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice Owls]] and the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Murphy was born in [[Durham, North Carolina]] to his mother, Albeda, and father, Kenneth Murphy Jr..{{Cite web|url=https://virginiasports.com/player/trey-murphy-iii/|title=Trey Murphy III|date=June 19, 2020|website=Virginia Cavaliers Official Athletic Site}} He played high school basketball at [[Cary Academy]] in [[Cary, North Carolina]] whereas a senior averaged 24.7 points and 7.4 rebounds per game while shooting 49.4% from the floor. He also shot 43.6% from beyond the three-point line and 85.8% from the free-throw stripe. On October 4, 2017, Murphy committed to play college basketball for [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Trey-Murphy-46040054/TimelineEvents/|title=Trey Murphy Timeline Events|website=247sports.com}} ==College career== ===Rice=== As a freshman, Murphy played in all 32 of Rice's games. He came off the bench 31 times and got to start one game, the first being against [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]] in March of 2019. He averaged 8.4 points and 2.6 rebounds. He ranked fourth in [[Conference USA]] (C-USA) in three-point field goal percentage (42.1%) and 14th in 3-pointers made per game (2.0).Set the school freshman record for three-point field goal percentage (42.1%). On January 26, 2019, Murphy scored a career-high of 24 points and five 3-pointers while going a career-best 6-of-6 from the free-throw line against UAB.{{Cite web|url=https://riceowls.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/trey-murphy-iii/5064|title=Trey Murphy III|website=Rice Owls}} As a sophomore, Murphy played in 29 of 32 games for Rice. He started in 23 of those games while coming off the bench in six. He led the Owls in scoring with 13.7 points and recorded 25 double-figure scoring games with two double-doubles. He also led the team with six 20-point games.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/trey-murphyiii-1.html|title=Trey Murphy III|website=Sports Reference}} ===Virginia=== On March 30, 2020, Murphy entered the transfer portal, and on April 14, 2020, he transferred to [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web|url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2020/04/16/mens-basketball-virginia-lands-transfer-trey-murphy-iii/|title=Virginia lands transfer Trey Murphy III|website=virginiasports.com|publisher=Virginia Sports|date=April 16, 2020|accessdate=April 12, 2021}} Cary, NC native, friend, and future teammate, Justin McKoy helped recruit him to Virginia.{{Cite web|url=https://wuvanews.com/meet-trey-murphy-iii/|title=Meet Trey Murphy III|website=WUVA News}} Due to [[COVID-19]] affecting college basketball, Murphy did not have to sit out a year and was granted three years of immediate eligibility instead of two. Coming off the bench, Murphy scored 21 points while shooting 7-of-9 from the field in the Cavaliers' season opener in [[Bubbleville]]. He made his first start against [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]] in late December 2020 and started the remainder of the season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/4397688/trey-murphy-iii|title=Gamelog|website=ESPN}} Murphy had an underrated year with Virginia, but the NBA scouts saw him as a top 45 NBA draft prospect.{{Cite web|url=https://augustafreepress.com/weekend-observations-juzang-trey-murphy-iii-vmi-heartbreaker/|title=Weekend Observations: Juzang, Trey Murphy III, VMI heartbreaker|website=Augusta Free Press}} On April 13, 2021, Murphy declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2021/4/13/22381878/trey-murphy-iii-virginia-mens-basketball-acc-nba-draft|title=Trey Murphy III announces decision to enter NBA Draft, maintain eligibility|website=https:www.streakingthelawn.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=April 13, 2021|accessdate=April 13, 2021}} On June 21, 2021, Murphy announced that he signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility with Virginia and ending his collegiate career.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Projected first-round pick Trey Murphy forgoes eligibility at Virginia, remains in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31681693/projected-first-round-pick-trey-murphy-forgoes-eligibility-virginia-remains-nba-draft?platform=amp&__twitter_impression=true
